claim: KDE's foreground booster sets CPUWeight on an app's systemd scope by a runtime set-property, and systemd applies that value straight to the cgroup rather than merging the unit's drop-ins again. So a CPUWeight drop-in under ~/.config/systemd/user for an app scope does not hold, however it is named and although systemd lists it in DropInPaths. Such a drop-in holds only between a daemon-reload and the next time that app gains or loses focus. Naming the file to sort after the booster's own does not help, because sort order decides a merge and the booster does not merge. Anyone wanting an app to keep a share against the focused window needs a lever the booster does not write: its own slice, or the booster's boost lowered for every app.

evidence:
Measured on the workstation on 2026-09-21, against the Spotify flatpak's scope.

The booster is /usr/bin/foreground_booster, run by plasma-foreground-booster.service, from rpm kcgroups-dmemcg-0.1-2.fc44. Its strings hold `weight to default`, `times normal weight` and `setCpuWeight`. No config file of its own was on the machine: ~/.config/kcgroupsrc did not exist.

What the booster does to a share: with Chromium focused, app.slice held app-org.chromium.Chromium-2460549.scope at cpu.weight 10000 while app-flatpak-com.spotify.Client-1854844264.scope held 100, the weight systemd ships. Every other child of app.slice, the code editor and Steam among them, also held 100.

How the booster writes it: /run/user/1000/systemd/transient/app-flatpak-com.spotify.Client-1854844264.scope.d/50-CPUWeight.conf held `[Scope]` and `CPUWeight=` — the empty form, which puts the share back to the default.

The drop-in was listed and still did not hold. `systemctl --user show -p DropInPaths` for the scope named both the booster's transient 50-CPUWeight.conf and ~/.config/systemd/user/app-flatpak-com.spotify.Client-.scope.d/90-share.conf, which held CPUWeight=5000. With both listed, `show -p CPUWeight` answered `[not set]` and the cgroup's cpu.weight read 100. A dashed-prefix drop-in directory does reach a transient scope, so that part works.

A daemon-reload made it hold, and one set-property took it away again. After `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, CPUWeight read 5000 and cpu.weight read 5000. Then `systemctl --user set-property --runtime <scope> CPUWeight=`, which is what the booster runs on focus loss, put cpu.weight back to 100 with the 90- drop-in still in place. `CPUWeight=10000` put it at 10000, and the empty form again put it at 100.
